title: a ticket a gate refuses waits in the trouble lane and posts to no design verb
intention: A ticket a gate refuses waits in the trouble lane CC and Akien read: Ticket.failed raises one trouble on the ticket naming the gate and every lack and never posts to a design verb, and the trouble clears when that gate later passes the ticket.
why: Measured 2026-11-11: every refusal posted machines/design/queueme to codemother, which declares no such verb, so each bounce raised two troubles (ticket-unqueued-<id>-at-design on the ticket and mail-codemother-has-no-verb-machines-design-queueme, 7x) and neither named the lacks. Akien, Q#85 (outline 3.3.4): design is CC and Akien until the outline is implemented; a refused ticket waits in the trouble lane, and nothing posts to a design verb no machine answers.
traces_to: press_office/CairnComponentOutline.txt 3.3.4 (Q#85); Law 7; Law 1. Supersedes the design-request part of 152d76785229 clause 4, fa4462c803d6 clauses 3, 4 and 7, and 386ea8131006 clause 2.
how: ticket.py failed(lacks, ..., gate=None): keep the FIXME kick-back (or the stand-still before repair) and the harbor post; then raise ticket-refused-<id>-at-<gate> (gate = kwarg, else lacks[0]['kind']) with detail {fileref, gate, lacks, workflow}; return {queued: False, gate, trouble, workflow}. DESIGN and both queueme(DESIGN) calls leave, and the module docstring says a fail waits in the trouble lane. queueme(): when the reply says passed true and ticket-refused-<id>-at-<gate> stands raised on the ticket's trail, clear it. chart_gate/gate.py answers trouble=got.get('trouble') in place of design_queued. Teeth: test_a_ticket_queues_itself_at_a_gate.py renames its two fail teeth and adds a clear tooth; chart_gate's _assert_design_asked becomes _assert_refused_trouble; watchme's tooth 2 asserts no request and the refused trouble.

clauses.claim: failed([two lacks]) from [BUILDME] puts the cursor at FIXME with both lacks as its fixme, posts one harbor crossing with direction back, sends no request at all, raises ticket-refused-<id>-at-<the first lack's kind> whose detail names both lacks, and returns queued false with that trouble
failed([one lack], gate='survey') from [TICKETME] leaves the cursor and the journal unchanged, writes the lack as the fixme, posts nothing, sends no request, and raises ticket-refused-<id>-at-survey
after a refusal at gate_x, queueme('gate_x') with a reply accepted true and passed false leaves ticket-refused-<id>-at-gate_x standing, and a reply accepted true and passed true clears it
the chart gate's refusal of a ticket and the watchme gate's red finding each send no request to any verb and raise ticket-refused-<id>-at-<stage or watchme>

decisions.text: D1: the trouble's gate comes from a gate= keyword, else the first lack's kind, so neither caller needs an edit to name it: the chart gate's lacks carry the stage and the watchme gate's carry 'watchme'. The clear rides queueme because that is where a gate's pass arrives; a ticket the watchme gate refused clears when its next gate passes it at that name, or by hand. chart_gate's design_queued becomes trouble, since it would read False forever.

measured.saw: 7 ticket-unqueued-*-at-design raises under ~/.cairn/logs/ticket/0/; mail-codemother-has-no-verb-machines-design-queueme standing at 7x; design_queued has one writer and no reader
measured.how: grep over ~/.cairn/logs/ticket/0/ and the session-open trouble lane; grep -rn design_queued over cairn/ and skills/
